notes.ios:
ReFineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services.

There is no account to demonstrate. The app has no login, no server, no registration, and collects no data. Nothing in it sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password we can supply: none exists.

What the app needs is the card itself. A FINEID card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency to one named citizen, in the same category as a passport. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we are unable to put one in the reviewer's hands.

Verifiable without a card, on this build:
- The app launches to its setup screen and reports what it needs rather than failing.
- The camera button beside the card access number opens a scanner for the QR code printed on the card.
- Entering any card access number and basic code and tapping "Read Certificate from Card" opens the system NFC scan sheet. It then waits for a card to be held against the phone, which is the hardware we cannot ship.
- Every screen is available in English, Finnish and Swedish, and with VoiceOver, larger text, and the dark interface.

This build reads the card and publishes its certificate to the system. It does not sign documents; that is the Mac app.
The complete source is public at https://github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple, including the card protocol, so the behaviour behind the card can be read directly.

If a demonstration mode is the expected remedy for an app whose hardware is a personal identity document, please say so and we will add one.
notes.macos:
ReFineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services.

There is no account to demonstrate. The app has no login, no server, no registration, and collects no data. Nothing in it sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password we can supply: none exists.

What the app needs is the card itself. A FINEID card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency to one named citizen, in the same category as a passport. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we are unable to put one in the reviewer's hands.

Verifiable without a card, on this build:
- The app launches and reports "Present your identity card to the reader" rather than failing.
- The bundled CryptoTokenKit token extension registers with the system on first launch and appears in the smart-card system's driver list with no card present. That registration is the product's whole purpose.
- Settings contains the PIN pane, which shows the card's change and reset tasks and its attempt counters, and the time-stamp authority list used when signing a document.
- Every screen is available in English, Finnish and Swedish, and with VoiceOver, larger text, and the dark interface.

The app makes outbound connections for one purpose: an archival signature fetches a qualified time stamp and the revocation data proving its chain. It binds no listening socket.
The complete source is public at https://github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple, including the card protocol, so the behaviour behind the card can be read directly.

If a demonstration mode is the expected remedy for an app whose hardware is a personal identity document, please say so and we will add one.

description.macos:
A reader for the Finnish identity card.

Insert your identity card into a USB smart-card reader and sign in to e-services directly in Safari with the certificate on your card. Drop a PDF on ReFineID to sign it with a qualified signature.

ReFineID is open source: github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple
description.ios:
ReFineID brings the Finnish identity card to iPhone and iPad.

Read your card with a USB-C smart-card reader, or wirelessly on iPhone, then sign in to e-services directly in Safari with the certificate on your card.

ReFineID is open source: github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple
